Along δ-parallel lines the nonempty intervals all acquire length 2||δ|| in the extrusion. The projection is unchanged, including the dimension-one convention, so the volume reserve follows by integration. For any fixed halfspace a translated interval changes the captured halfline length by at most ||δ||, while a full or empty line is unchanged. This yields an absolute mass difference rather than a one-sided comparison.

The symmetric reference D has half its mass in every proper closed cap through its center. Combining the translation error and volume reserve proves the factor 1/2, attained by the translated box example with middle extrusion. The midpoint of the two given endpoints is the translated box, contained in the middle. The zero-defect case follows directly.

An affine center map cancels in every anchored representation, leaving defect tδ. The segment contains that translate for each t in [-1,1]. Grouping a hull combination by its bases gives exactly the prescribed sections and lattice completeness excludes new integer bases. Spanning bases and a full-dimensional continuous fiber give interior.
